name: Number Transformation II
description: You are given a sequence of positive integers x 1 , x 2 , ..., x n and two non-negative integers a and b . Your task is to transform a into b . To do that, you can perform the following moves: subtract 1 from the current a ; subtract a mod x i (1 ≤ i ≤ n ) from the current a . Operation a mod x i means taking the remainder after division of number a by number x i . Now you want to know the minimum number of moves needed to transform a into b .
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer n ( 1 ≤ n ≤ 10 5 ). The second line contains n space-separated integers x 1 , x 2 , ..., x n ( 2 ≤ x i ≤ 10 9 ). The third line contains two integers a and b ( 0  ≤ b ≤ a ≤ 10 9 , a - b ≤ 10 6 ).
output_specification: Print a single integer — the required minimum number of moves needed to transform number a into number b .
approach_summary: Identify exchange argument or greedy choice property. Sort elements by payoff ratio or deadline and greedily pick candidates to achieve global optimum.
